Information about our Executive Officers
paragraphs: Our company, Franklin Street Properties Corp., which we refer to as FSP Corp., the Company, we or our, is a Maryland corporation that operates in a manner intended to qualify as a real estate investment trust, or REIT, for federal income tax purposes. Our common stock is traded on the NYSE American under the symbol "FSP". FSP Corp. is the successor to Franklin Street Partners Limited Partnership, or the FSP Partnership, which was originally formed as a Massachusetts general partnership in January 1997 as the successor to a Massachusetts general partnership that was formed in 1981. On January 1, 2002, the FSP Partnership converted into FSP Corp., which we refer to as the conversion. As a result of this conversion, the FSP Partnership ceased to exist and we succeeded to the business of the FSP Partnership. In the conversion, each unit of both general and limited partnership interests in the FSP Partnership was converted into one share of our common stock. As a result of the conversion, we hold, directly and indirectly, 100% of the interest in three former subsidiaries of the FSP Partnership: FSP Investments LLC, FSP Property Management LLC, and FSP Holdings LLC. We operate some of our business through these subsidiaries.

We are a REIT focused on commercial real estate investments primarily in office markets and currently operate in only one segment: real estate operations. The principal revenue sources for our real estate operations include rental income from real estate leasing, property dispositions and fee income from asset/property management and development.

Our current strategy is to focus on infill and central business district office properties in the United States sunbelt and mountain west regions as well as select opportunistic markets. We believe that the United States sunbelt and mountain west regions have macro-economic drivers that have the potential to increase occupancies and rents. We are focused on long-term growth and appreciation.

Previously we also operated in an investment banking segment, which was discontinued in December 2011. Our investment banking segment generated brokerage commissions, loan origination fees, development services and other fees related to the organization of single-purpose REITs that own real estate and the private placement of equity in those entities.

From time-to-time we may acquire real estate or invest in real estate by making secured loans on real estate. We may also pursue on a selective basis the sale of our properties to take advantage of the value creation and demand for our properties, or for geographic or property specific reasons.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned and operated a portfolio of real estate consisting of 14 properties, which we refer to as our owned properties. We derive rental revenue from income paid to us by tenants of these properties. See Item 2 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for more information about our properties. From time-to-time we dispose of properties generating gains or losses in an ongoing effort to improve and upgrade our portfolio and/or to repay a portion of our debt.

We provide asset management, property management, property accounting, investor and/or development services to our portfolio and our Sponsored REIT through our subsidiaries FSP Investments LLC and FSP Property Management LLC. Neither FSP Investments LLC nor FSP Property Management LLC receives any rental income.

We had a non-controlling common stock interest in the corporation that was the sole member of FSP Monument Circle LLC, which we refer to as the Sponsored REIT or Monument Circle. The Sponsored REIT was organized to operate as a real estate investment trust and was consolidated in our financial statements effective January 1, 2023. The
property held by the Sponsored REIT was sold on June 6, 2025 and Monument Circle and the corporation that had been its sole member were dissolved on December 9, 2025.

As an owner of commercial real estate, a sector with significant environmental, social and governance, or ESG, impact, we strive to maximize shareholder value through the prudent application of sound ESG strategies. Our efforts have been awarded recognition from various third party review entities, such as GRESB, ENERGY STAR and LEED.

Uncertainty still surrounds the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the commercial real estate market and our business. Many of our tenants still do not fully occupy the space that they lease. The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic continues to present material uncertainty and risk with respect to the performance of our properties and our financial results, such as the potential negative impact to the businesses of our tenants, the impact of work-from-home and return-to-work policies, the potential negative impact to leasing efforts and occupancy at our properties, the occurrence of a default under any of our debt agreements, the potential for increased borrowing costs, negative impacts on our ability to refinance existing indebtedness or to secure new sources of capital on favorable terms, decreases in values of our real estate assets, and uncertainty regarding government and regulatory policy. We are unable to estimate the full extent of the long-term impact that the COVID-19 pandemic has had and will have on our future financial results at this time. See "Item 1A. Risk Factors" and "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" for additional information.

Our investment objectives are to increase shareholder value by increasing revenue from rental, interest and fee income and net gains from sales of properties. We expect that we will continue to derive real estate revenue from owned properties.

Although our property portfolio is focused on properties in the central business districts of Dallas, Denver, Houston and Minneapolis, we may acquire, and have acquired in the past, real properties in any geographic area of the United States and of any property type. Our 14 owned office properties are located in three different states as of December 31, 2025. See Item 2 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for more information about our properties. Our investment objectives are to create shareholder value by increasing revenue from rental, interest and fee income and net gains from sales of properties. We expect that we will continue to derive real estate revenue from owned properties and property management services. We may also acquire additional real properties.

As a result, from time to time, as market conditions warrant, we expect to sell properties owned by us. On June 6, 2025, we sold an office property located in Indianapolis, Indiana for a gross sale price of $6 million, at a loss of $12.9 million. On January 26, 2024, we sold an office property located in Richardson, Texas for a gross sales price of $35.0 million, at a loss of approximately $2.1 million. On July 8, 2024, we sold a property in Glen Allen, Virginia for a gross sales price of $31.0 million, at a loss of $13.2 million. On October 23, 2024, we sold an office property located in Atlanta, Georgia for a gross sales price of $34.0 million at a loss of $27.2 million. On March 10, 2023, we sold an office property located in Elk Grove, Illinois for a gross sales price of $29.1 million, at a gain of approximately $8.4 million. On August 9, 2023, we sold a property in Charlotte, North Carolina for a gross sales price of $9.2 million at a loss of $0.8 million. On October 26, 2023, we sold an office property located in Plano, Texas for a gross sales price of $48 million at a gain of $10.6 million. On December 6, 2023, we sold an office property located in Miami, Florida for a gross sales price of $68.0 million at a loss of approximately $18.9 million.

headings: Risks Related to our Operations and Properties
Economic conditions in the United States could have a material adverse impact on our earnings and financial condition.
If we are not able to collect sufficient rents from each of our owned real properties, we may suffer significant operating losses.
We may not be able to dispose of properties on acceptable terms or within the time periods we anticipate pursuant to our disposition strategy.
We face risks from tenant defaults or bankruptcies.
New acquisitions may fail to perform as expected.
We face risks in owning, developing, redeveloping and operating real property.
We may encounter significant delays in reletting vacant space, resulting in losses of income.
We face risks of tenant-type concentration.
We face risks from geographic concentration.
We compete with national, regional and local real estate operators and developers, which could adversely affect our cash flow.
We face possible risks associated with the physical effects of climate change.
Security breaches and other disruptions could compromise our information and expose us to liability, which could cause our business and reputation to suffer.
Actual or threatened terrorist attacks may adversely affect our ability to generate revenues and the value of our properties.
We may lose capital investment or anticipated profits if an uninsured event occurs.
Risks Related to our Indebtedness
Failure to comply with covenants in the Credit Agreement could adversely affect our financial condition.
Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Matters
We are subject to risks from changes in trade policies and tariffs
We are subject to possible liability relating to environmental matters, and we cannot assure you that we have identified all possible liabilities.
We are subject to compliance with the Americans With Disabilities Act and fire and safety regulations, any of which could require us to make significant capital expenditures.
We face risks associated with our tenants being designated "Prohibited Persons" by the Office of Foreign Assets Control.
Risks Related to our Common Stock
We have suspended quarterly dividends and may not resume paying dividends on our common stock, and may not elect to resume paying dividends in the foreseeable future or at all.
The real properties held by us may significantly decrease in value.
Further issuances of equity securities may be dilutive to current stockholders.
The price of our common stock may vary.
Risks Related to our Organization and Structure
Our employee retention plan may prevent changes in control.
We would incur adverse tax consequences if we failed to qualify as a REIT.
Provisions in our organizational documents may prevent changes in control.
paragraphs: The following material factors, among others, could cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated by forward-looking statements made in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and presented elsewhere by management from time-to-time.

The long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may continue to have an adverse impact on our financial condition and results of operations. This impact could be materially adverse to the extent that the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, or future pandemics, cause tenants to be unable to pay their rent or reduce the demand for commercial real estate, or cause other impacts described below.

The COVID-19 pandemic has adversely impacted our properties and operating results and continues to present material uncertainty and risk with respect to the performance of our properties and our financial results. Uncertainty still surrounds the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, on the commercial real estate market and our business. Many of our tenants still do not fully occupy the space that they lease. Any ongoing negative impacts from the COVID-19 pandemic could adversely affect us and/or our tenants due to, among other factors: the potential negative impact to the businesses of our tenants, the impact of work-from-home and return-to-work policies, the potential negative impact to leasing efforts and occupancy at our properties, the occurrence of a default under any of our debt agreements, the potential for increased borrowing costs, negative impacts on our ability to refinance existing indebtedness or to secure new sources of capital on favorable terms, decreases in values of our real estate assets, and uncertainty regarding government and regulatory policy.

Some of our existing tenants and potential tenants operate in businesses and industries that continue to be adversely affected by continuing effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. These effects could lead to increased rent delinquencies and/or defaults under leases, a lower demand for rentable space leading to increased concessions or lower occupancy, increased tenant improvement capital expenditures, or reduced rental rates to maintain occupancies. For example, on December 21, 2020, the parent company of a tenant that leased approximately 130,000 square feet filed a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, resulting in a writeoff charge of $3.1 million. Our operations could be materially negatively affected as a result, which could adversely affect our operating results, our ability to pay dividends, our ability to repay or refinance our existing indebtedness, and the price of our common stock.

The global economy continues to experience significant disruptions and uncertainty as a result of various factors, including changes in U.S. trade or other policies or those policies of other nations, geopolitical events such as the wars and conflicts in Iran and other countries in the Middle East and Ukraine, increasing tensions with China and Venezuela, tensions between the U.S. and Europe related to the sovereignty of Greenland, major political shifts domestically or internationally and continuing supply chain difficulties. Because economic conditions directly affect the demand for office space, our primary income producing asset, broad economic market conditions in the United States, including uncertainty over interest rates, inflation, tariffs, slower growth, stock market volatility or recession fears, could have a material adverse effect on our earnings and financial condition. Economic conditions may be affected by numerous other factors, including but not limited to, inflation and employment levels, energy prices, uncertainty about government fiscal, monetary, trade and tax policies, changes in currency exchange rates, the regulatory environment and the availability of credit. Future economic factors also may negatively affect the demand for office space, real estate values, occupancy levels and property income.

A substantial portion of our revenue is generated by the rental income of our real properties. If our properties do not provide us with a steady rental income, our revenues will decrease, which may cause us to incur operating losses in the future.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and notes thereto appearing elsewhere in this report. Historical results and percentage relationships set forth in the consolidated financial statements, including trends which might appear, should not be taken as necessarily indicative of future operations. The following discussion and other parts of this Annual Report on Form 10-K may also contain forward-looking statements based on current judgments and current knowledge of management, which are subject to certain risks, trends and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in such forward-looking statements. Accordingly, readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on forward-looking statements. Investors are cautioned that our forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainty, including without limitation, adverse changes in general economic or local market conditions, including as a result of the long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, wars, terrorist attacks or other acts of violence, which may negatively affect the markets in which we and our tenants operate, impacts of changes in tariffs that the United States and other countries have announced or implemented, as well as any additional new tariffs, trade restrictions or export regulations that may be implemented or reversed in the future, inflation rates, interest rates, disruptions in the debt markets, economic conditions in the markets in which we own properties, risks of a lessening of demand for the types of real estate owned by us, adverse changes in energy prices, which if sustained, could negatively impact occupancy and rental rates in the markets in which we own properties, including energy-influenced markets such as Dallas, Denver and Houston, expectations for future potential property dispositions, expectations for future potential leasing activity, changes in government regulations and regulatory uncertainty, uncertainty about governmental fiscal policy, geopolitical events and expenditures that cannot be anticipated, such as utility rate and usage increases, delays in construction schedules, unanticipated increases in construction costs, unanticipated repairs, increases in the level of general and administrative costs as a percentage of revenues as revenues decrease as a result of property dispositions, additional staffing, insurance increases and real estate tax valuation reassessments. See "Risk Factors" in Part I, Item 1A, of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Although we believe the expectations reflected in the forward-looking statements are reasonable, we cannot guarantee future results, levels of activity, acquisitions, dispositions, performance or achievements. We may not update any of the forward-looking statements after the date this Annual Report on Form 10-K is filed to conform them to actual results or to changes in our expectations that occur after such date, other than as required by law.

FSP Corp., or we or the Company, operates in a single reportable segment: real estate operations. The real estate operations market involves real estate rental operations, leasing, secured financing of real estate and services provided for asset management, property management, property acquisitions, dispositions and development. Our current strategy is to focus on infill and central business district office properties in the United States sunbelt and mountain west regions as well as select opportunistic markets. We believe that the United States sunbelt and mountain west regions have macro-economic drivers that have the potential to increase occupancies and rents. We are focused on long-term growth and appreciation.
As of December 31, 2025, all of our total owned portfolio, consisting of approximately 4.8 million square feet, was located in Dallas, Denver, Houston and Minneapolis.

The main factor that affects our real estate operations is the broad economic market conditions in the United States. These market conditions affect the occupancy levels and the rent levels on both a national and local level. We have no influence on broader economic market conditions. We may look to acquire and/or develop quality properties in good locations in order to lessen the impact of downturns in the market and to take advantage of upturns when they occur.
In May 2025, we announced that our Board of Directors had initiated a review of strategic alternatives in order to explore ways to maximize shareholder value.
Throughout the strategic review process, the Board of Directors and management directed its financial advisors to evaluate a broad range of strategic alternatives, including:
• Portfolio-level transactions • Individual asset dispositions • Joint venture structures • Corporate-level transactions
• Liquidation scenarios • Refinancing alternatives
During the period from the commencement of the strategic review process to the date of this Annual Report:
• Transaction volume across many of our primary submarkets remained historically low.
• Where transactions occurred, activity was frequently concentrated in lender-controlled or distressed situations and at pricing levels not reflective of stabilized intrinsic valuations.

• Institutional capital in the office sector remained highly selective nationally, primarily targeting trophy or newly delivered assets in select gateway markets, or deeply discounted properties in distress scenarios. As a result, reported transaction pricing may be influenced by a limited number of transactions that are not necessarily reflective of actual achievable values on our assets.

• Lending liquidity for office assets in similar markets and with comparable occupancy profiles and lease maturities has been significantly constrained relative to historical norms, further limiting the ability to execute transactions at pricing levels consistent with long-term asset values.

On February 26, 2026, we closed a $320 million secured credit facility with an affiliate of TPG Credit. We repaid in full all of our then outstanding approximately $249 million aggregate principal amount of indebtedness with borrowings under the facility. The facility has an original stated maturity of February 26, 2029, subject to potential extension of up to one year at our option, subject to certain conditions. The facility consists of (i) initial term loans in an aggregate principal amount of $275 million, and (ii) delayed draw term loans available upon the approval of the lenders party thereto in an aggregate principal amount of up to $45 million. The delayed draw term loans may be used, subject to certain conditions, to fund tenant improvements, leasing commissions, building improvements and other uses approved by the lender. See Note 12, Subsequent Events, of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements contained in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further information on the Credit Agreement.

paragraphs: 本公司為Franklin Street Properties Corp.，我們簡稱為FSP Corp.、本公司、我們或我們的，為一間馬裏蘭州公司，其營運方式旨在符合美國聯邦所得稅法規之不動產投資信託（REIT）之規定。本公司普通股於紐約證券交易所美國市場（NYSE American）交易，代碼為"FSP"。FSP Corp.為Franklin Street Partners Limited Partnership（簡稱FSP Partnership）之繼承者，該FSP Partnership最初於1997年1月成立為一間馬薩諸塞州普通合夥企業，為一間於1981年成立之馬薩諸塞州普通合夥企業之繼承者。於2002年1月1日，FSP Partnership轉換為FSP Corp.，我們簡稱為轉換。此轉換後，FSP Partnership不再存在，本公司繼承FSP Partnership之業務。於轉換時，FSP Partnership之所有普通合夥與有限合夥權益單位皆轉換為本公司之普通股一股。此轉換後，本公司直接與間接持有FSP Partnership之三個前子公司100%之權益：FSP Investments LLC、FSP Property Management LLC及FSP Holdings LLC。本公司透過這些子公司運作部分業務。
本公司為專注於商業不動產投資之REIT，主要投資於辦公室市場，目前僅經營一個應報告分部：不動產運營。本公司不動產運營之主要收入來源包括不動產租賃之租金收入、不動產處分收入及資產/不動產管理與開發之費用收入。
本公司目前之策略為專注於美國陽光帶與山脈西部地區之填補與市中心辦公室不動產，以及部分機會性市場。我們認為美國陽光帶與山脈西部地區具有總體經濟驅動因素，有潛力提高租賃率與租金。本公司專注於長期成長與資產增值。
先前本公司亦經營投資銀行業務分部，該分部於2011年12月終止。投資銀行業務分部產生證券經紀佣金、貸款發放手續費、開發服務及其他與組織單一用途REIT之費用，該REIT擁有不動產，並進行該等實體之權益私募發行。
本公司有時會透過對不動產提供擔保貸款方式取得不動產或投資於不動產。本公司亦可能根據選擇性考量出售本公司之不動產，以利用本公司不動產之價值創造與需求，或因地理或不動產特定因素。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有並運營一組不動產投資組合，包含14處不動產，我們簡稱為本公司擁有之不動產。本公司從這些不動產之租戶支付給本公司之收入中取得租金收入。請參閱本年度10-K表報表第2項以取得更多有關本公司不動產之資訊。本公司有時會處分不動產，產生獲利或虧損，以持續改善與升級本公司投資組合及/或償還部分債務。
本公司透過子公司FSP Investments LLC與FSP Property Management LLC為本公司投資組合與 Sponsored REIT 提供資產管理、不動產管理、不動產會計、投資者及/或開發服務。FSP Investments LLC與FSP Property Management LLC均不收取租金收入。
本公司持有FSP Monument Circle LLC之非控制性普通股權益，該公司為Sponsored REIT（簡稱Monument Circle），Sponsored REIT設立為運作不動產投資信託，自2023年1月1日起，本公司財務報表已將Sponsored REIT合併。
由受託REIT持有的資產於2025年6月6日出售，Monument Circle及曾為其唯一成員的公司於2025年12月9日解散。
作為商業不動產所有者，此產業對環境、社會及治理，或ESG，有重大影響，我們致力於透過審慎應用良好的ESG策略來最大化股東價值。我們的努力已獲得多個第三方評審機構的認可，例如GRESB、ENERGY STAR及LEED。

有關新型冠狀病毒疫情對商業不動產市場及我們業務的長期影響仍存在不確定性。許多租戶尚未完全佔用其租賃空間。新型冠狀病毒疫情的影響持續對我們的不動產及財務結果產生重大不確定性與風險，例如對租戶業務的潛在負面影響、遠距辦公及回歸辦公政策的影響、對我們不動產租賃努力及佔用率的潛在負面影響、任何債務協議下發生違約的情況、借款成本增加的潛在風險、對我們重組現有債務或以有利條件取得新資金來源能力的負面影響、我們不動產資產價值的下降，以及政府與監管政策的不確定性。我們目前無法估計新型冠狀病毒疫情對我們未來財務結果的長期影響範圍。請參閱「項目1A. 風險因素」及「項目7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析」以取得更多資訊。
我們的投資目標為透過增加租金、利息及費用收入以及出售不動產的淨獲利來提高股東價值。我們預期將持續從自有不動產中取得不動產收入。

儘管我們的不動產組合專注於達拉斯、丹佛、休士頓及明尼阿波利斯等市中心的不動產，我們可能取得，且過去已取得，美國任何地理區域及任何類型的不動產。截至2025年12月31日，我們的14處自有辦公室不動產位於三個不同的州。請參閱本年度報告10-K表單第2項以取得更多關於我們不動產的資訊。我們的投資目標為透過增加租金、利息及費用收入以及出售不動產的淨獲利來創造股東價值。我們預期將持續從自有不動產及不動產管理服務中取得不動產收入。我們也可能取得更多不動產。

因應此，視市場狀況而定，我們預期會出售我們所有的不動產。於 2025 年 6 月 6 日，我們出售位於印第安那州印第安納波利斯的辦公室不動產，總售價為 6 百萬美元，產生虧損 12.9 百萬美元。於 2024 年 1 月 26 日，我們出售位於德克薩斯州理查森的辦公室不動產，總售價為 35.0 百萬美元，產生虧損約 2.1 百萬美元。於 2024 年 7 月 8 日，我們出售位於維吉尼亞州格倫艾倫的不動產，總售價為 31.0 百萬美元，產生虧損 13.2 百萬美元。於 2024 年 10 月 23 日，我們出售位於喬治亞州亞特蘭大的辦公室不動產，總售價為 34.0 百萬美元，產生虧損 27.2 百萬美元。於 2023 年 3 月 10 日，我們出售位於伊利諾州艾爾克格羅夫的辦公室不動產，總售價為 29.1 百萬美元，產生獲利約 8.4 百萬美元。於 2023 年 8 月 9 日，我們出售位於北卡羅萊納州夏洛特的不動產，總售價為 9.2 百萬美元，產生虧損 0.8 百萬美元。於 2023 年 10 月 26 日，我們出售位於德克薩斯州普蘭諾的辦公室不動產，總售價為 48 百萬美元，產生獲利 10.6 百萬美元。於 2023 年 12 月 6 日，我們出售位於佛羅裏達州邁阿密的辦公室不動產，總售價為 68.0 百萬美元，產生虧損約 18.9 百萬美元。

paragraphs: 下列討論應與本報告中其他處所出現的財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。歷史結果及財務報表中所列示的百分比關係，包括可能出現的趨勢，不應被視為必然反映未來營運情況。下列討論及其他部分本年度10-K表報表亦可能包含基於管理層當前判斷及知識的展望性陳述，這些陳述受到某些風險、趨勢及不確定性影響，可能導致實際結果與這些展望性陳述所顯示者有重大差異。因此，讀者應謹慎勿過度依賴展望性陳述。投資人應知悉，我們的展望性陳述涉及風險與不確定性，包括但不限於總體經濟或當地市場條件的惡化，包括因 COVID-19 大流行長期影響、戰爭、恐怖攻擊或其他暴力行為所導致的變化，可能對我們及我們租戶所從事的市場產生負面影響，美國及其他國家所宣佈或實施的關稅變動的影響，以及未來可能實施或廢除的任何新關稅、貿易限制或出口規範，通貨膨脹率、利率、債務市場中斷、我們擁有不動產的市場經濟條件、我們所擁有不動產類型需求減少的風險、能源價格的惡化變動，若持續不變，可能對我們擁有不動產的市場的佔有率及租金產生負面影響，包括受能源影響的市場如達拉斯、丹佛及休士頓，未來潛在不動產處分的預期、未來潛在租賃活動的預期、政府規範的變化及規範不確定性、政府財政政策的不確定性、地緣政治事件及無法預見的支出，如電力費用及使用量增加、建設進度延誤、未預見的建設成本增加、未預見的修繕費用、一般及行政成本佔收入百分比增加，因不動產處分導致收入減少，額外人力配置、保險費用增加及不動產稅評價重新評估。

FSP Corp.，或我們或本公司，從事單一應報告分部：不動產營運。不動產營運市場涉及不動產租賃營運、租賃、不動產 secured financing 及為資產管理、不動產管理、不動產取得、處分及開發所提供的服務。我們目前的策略是專注於美國太陽帶及山脈西部地區的市中心辦公室不動產以及選擇性的機會市場。我們認為美國太陽帶及山脈西部地區具有總體經濟動力，有潛力提高佔有率及租金。我們專注於長期成長與增值。
截至2025年12月31日，我們所有總擁有不動產組合，約為4.8百萬平方英尺，均位於達拉斯、丹佛、休士頓及明尼阿波利斯。
影響我們不動產營運的主要因素是美國廣泛的經濟市場條件。這些市場條件會影響佔有率及租金水平，無論是國家層面或地方層面。我們對廣泛的經濟市場條件毫無影響。我們可能尋求取得或開發優質不動產於良好地點，以減輕市場低迷的影響，並在市場上漲時把握機會。
2025年5月，我們宣佈我們董事會已啟動戰略替代方案的審查，以探討如何最大化股東價值。
在戰略審查過程中，董事會及管理層指示其財務顧問評估廣泛的戰略替代方案，包括：
• 組合層面交易 • 個別資產處分 • 合資企業結構 • 公司層面交易
• 液化情境 • 再融資替代方案
自戰略評估程序啟動至本年度報告日之期間：
• 我們許多主要次級市場之交易量持續處於歷史低點。
• 交易發生時，活動頻繁集中於貸款人控制或資產處於困境之情境，且價格水準未能反映穩定之內在價值。
• 房地產業務之機構資金持續 nationally 高度選擇性，主要針對特定門戶市場之冠軍資產或新交付資產，或處於困境情境之深度折扣資產。因此，報導之交易價格可能受極少數交易影響，未必反映我們資產實際可達之價值。
• 在類似市場且具有可比佔用率及租約到期日之辦公室資產之貸款流動性，相較歷史常態顯著受限，進一步限制執行交易之能力，使其價格水準無法符合長期資產價值。

2026 年 2 月 26 日，我們與 TPG Credit 之附屬公司簽訂一筆 320 百萬美元之 secured credit facility。我們以該融資之貸款償還當時約 249 百萬美元之總本金金額之債務。該融資之原始 stated maturity 為 2029 年 2 月 26 日，並可由我們選擇延長最多一年，但須符合特定條件。該融資包含 (i) 初始期貸款總本金金額為 275 百萬美元，以及 (ii) 延遲提款期貸款，經貸款人同意後可提取總本金金額最高為 45 百萬美元。延遲提款期貸款可用於經貸款人批准之租客改善、租賃佣金、建築改善及其他用途。有關 Credit Agreement 之進一步資訊，請參見本年度報告 10-K 表單之 Part II, Item 8 所附財務會計彙編註釋之 Note 12, Subsequent Events。

headings: 與我們營運及資產相關的風險
美國經濟狀況可能對我們的獲利及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
若我們無法自各項自有不動產取得足夠租金，我們可能面臨顯著的營運虧損。
我們可能無法依照我們處置策略預期的條件或時間內處置不動產。
我們面臨租戶違約或破產的風險。
新進購的資產可能無法如預期般表現。
我們在擁有、開發、重新開發及營運不動產方面面臨風險。
我們可能遭遇重新出租空置空間的重大延誤，導致收入損失。
本公司面臨租戶集中度風險。
本公司面臨地理集中度風險。
本公司與全國性、區域性及地方性不動產經營者及開發商競爭，此情形可能不利於本公司現金流。
本公司可能面臨與氣候變遷實體影響相關之風險。
資訊安全事件及其他中斷情形可能影響本公司資訊，使本公司面臨法律責任，此情形可能導致本公司業務與聲譽受損。
實際或威脅性恐怖攻擊可能不利於本公司產生收入之能力及不動產價值。
若發生未投保事件，本公司可能喪失資本投資或預期獲利。
與本公司負債相關之風險
未能遵守信用協議中的約定條款可能會對我們的財務狀況造成不利影響。
與法律及法規事項相關的風險
我們面臨因貿易政策及關稅變動而產生的風險
我們可能因環境事項而面臨責任，且我們無法保證已識別所有可能的責任。
我們需遵守美國殘障法案及防火與安全規範，任何一項都可能要求我們進行重大資本支出。
我們面臨因租戶被美國財產管制辦公室指定為『禁止人士』而產生的風險。
與我們普通股相關的風險
我們已暫停發放季節性股息，可能不會恢復支付普通股股息，且可能在可預見的未來或完全不會恢復支付股息。
本公司所持有的實質不動產可能大幅減值。
進一步發行權益證券可能對現有股東造成稀釋。
本公司普通股的價格可能波動。
與本公司組織與結構相關的風險
本公司員工保留計畫可能防止控制權變更。
若本公司未能符合REIT的條件，將導致不利的稅務後果。
本公司組織章程中的條款可能防止控制權變更。
paragraphs: 下列因素，包括但不限於，可能會導致實際結果與本年度10-K表報表中所做之預測性陳述及管理階層不時於其他地方所作之預測性陳述有重大差異。
冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情的長期影響可能持續對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。此影響可能對我們造成重大不利，若冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情或其他未來疫情的長期影響導致租戶無法支付租金或減少商業不動產需求，或造成下列所描述的其他影響。

冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情已對我們的不動產及營運成果造成不利影響，並持續對我們不動產的表現及財務結果產生重大不確定性與風險。冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情的長期影響對商業不動產市場及我們業務的不確定性仍然存在。許多租戶仍未完全佔用其所租用的空間。冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情持續產生的負面影響可能對我們及/或租戶造成不利影響，原因包括但不限於：租戶業務可能受到的負面影響、遠距辦公及回歸辦公政策的影響、我們不動產租賃努力及佔用率可能受到的負面影響、任何債務協議下發生違約、借款成本可能增加、對我們重組現有債務或以有利條件取得新資金來源的負面影響、我們不動產資產價值的下降，以及政府與監管政策的不確定性。

部分現有租戶及潛在租戶所從事的業務及產業持續受到冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情持續影響，這些影響可能導致租金逾期或違約，租賃空間需求減少導致讓利增加或佔用率下降，租戶改善資本支出增加，或為維持佔用率而降低租金率。例如，2020年12月21日，一名租戶所屬之母公司（租賃約130,000平方英呎）提出根據美國破產法第11章之救濟申請，導致產生3.1百萬美元之寫損費用。我們的營運可能因此受到重大負面影響，可能對我們營運成果、支付股息能力、償還或重組現有債務能力，以及普通股價格造成不利影響。

全球經濟持續因多種因素而面臨重大幹擾與不確定性，包括美國貿易或其他政策或他國政策的變動、地緣政治事件如伊朗及其他中東國家及烏克蘭的戰爭與衝突、與中國及委內瑞拉的關係緊張、美國與歐洲之間關於格陵蘭主權的緊張關係、國內或國際的重大政治變動，以及持續的供應鏈困難。因經濟狀況直接影響辦公室空間需求，而辦公室空間為我們的主要收入來源，美國廣泛經濟市場狀況，包括對利率、通貨膨脹、關稅、較慢成長、股市波動或經濟衰退的擔憂，可能對我們的獲利及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。經濟狀況可能受到多種其他因素影響，包括但不限於通貨膨脹與就業水平、能源價格、對政府財政、貨幣、貿易及稅收政策的不確定性、貨幣兌換率變動、監管環境及信貸可得性。
我們收入的相當大一部分來自於不動產租金收入。若我們的不動產無法提供穩定的租金收入，我們的收入將減少，這可能導致我們未來產生營運虧損。
